page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, translating to a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It features hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instructions. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2923.69. However, its multi-core CPU performance is weaker, falling into the bottom 25% with a score of 5862.86. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, measuring 51.54 GB/sec for read-only operations and 38.79 GB/sec for write operations, while small cached block reads are weak at 273.99 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, but multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with clang fall into the bottom 25%.

Given its hardware profile and performance characteristics, the c2d-standard-4 is suitable for workloads that rely heavily on single-core execution rather than highly parallelized multi-core processing. Appropriate workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and moderate web serving, though static web serving throughput is relatively low at 5.46 GB/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide predictable execution for single-threaded tasks, but the resource density and lower multi-core scaling make it less optimal for dense database operations or parallelized build pipelines.

It contains 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core and a 32 MB L3 cache, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, ranking in the top 25%, while multi-core performance and memory bandwidth for small cached blocks fall into the bottom 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression tasks perform at an average level. This instance is best suited for workloads prioritizing single-threaded execution, such as basic text processing, lightweight web serving, and simple application hosting, rather than highly parallelized database operations or multi-threaded compilation tasks.
